## Problem description

This puzzle, published by Mickaël Launay [@lemonde2026jungle], reads as follows. 

Players $A$ and $B$ are initially on different starting nodes, on the following graph:

![Illustration from [@lemonde2026jungle]](images/jungle.png){width=50% fig-align="center"}

The goal is to find the minimum time and the meeting node such that:

- at each time step $t \to t+1$, both players must move to an adjacent node (stationary waiting is prohibited);
- each edge traversal represents exactly one unit of time;
- when meeting, both players must occupy the same node;
- passing each other on a trail is not a valid meeting, the rendez-vous must occur at a node.


## MIP model

#### Parameters

- $K=\{A,B\}$: set of players 
- $V$: nodes of the graph
- $N(v)$: set of adjacent nodes of node $v \in V$
- $s(k) \in V$: starting point of player $k \in K$
- $T$: set of days

#### Variables

- $\textcolor{blue}{x}_{v,t}^k \in \{0,1\}$: takes value $1$ if and only if player $k\in K$ is on node $v\in V$ on day $t\in T$
- $\textcolor{blue}{z}_{v,t} \in \{0,1\}$: takes value $1$ if and only if players meet on node $v\in V$ on day $t\in T$
- $\textcolor{blue}{y}_{t} \in \{0,1\}$: takes value $1$ if and only if players meet on day $t\in T$

#### Objective function

To find the earlist meeting day, we maximize the meeting time:

$$
\max \sum_{t \in T}\textcolor{blue}{y}_t
$$

subject to:

#### Constraints

- On each day, players are on exactly one node:

$$
\sum_{v \in V} \textcolor{blue}{x}_{v,t}^k=1 \quad \forall t \in T, \forall k\in K
$$

- Enforce the starting points:

$$
\textcolor{blue}{x}_{s(k),1}^k=1 \quad \forall k \in K
$$

- Connexity rules: if a node $v$ is reached on day $t$, then it must have been on one of its neighbors the day before:

$$
\textcolor{blue}{x}_{v,t}^k \le \sum_{u \in N(v)} \textcolor{blue}{x}_{u,t-1}^k \quad \forall k \in K, \forall t>1
$$

- If node $v$ is a meeting day on day $t$, then $A$ and $B$ must meet there, at that time: 

$$
\textcolor{blue}{z}_{v,t} \le \textcolor{blue}{x}_{v,t}^k \quad \forall v \in V,\forall t \in T, \forall k \in K
$$

- If day $t$ is a meeting day, then one of the nodes must be a meeting point on that day:

$$
\textcolor{blue}{y}_{t} \le \sum_{v \in V} \textcolor{blue}{z}_{v,t} \quad \forall t \in T
$$
